analysis_trace: Trial NCT05384132 is a randomized single-blind parallel study evaluating Livfresh Dental Gel (LDG) containing EDTA as adjunct to SRP vs standard fluoride dentifrice in Stage II-III periodontitis patients. Primary endpoint: incremental PD reduction at Day 180 for sites with PD>4mm. Secondary endpoints: GI, PI, BOP reductions. No direct results available (expected 2027). Evidence from similar EDTA dentifrice study (J Periodontol 2021, PMID 33331040) showed significant PD reduction in Stage I-II maintenance patients, supporting LDG mechanism. EDTA prevents bacterial adhesion, potentially enhancing SRP outcomes. Population differences (maintenance vs active treatment) and lack of direct Phase data limit precision. SRP alone achieves 1-2mm PD reduction; adjunctive therapies typically add 0.3-0.5mm incremental benefit. GI/PI/BOP endpoints are responsive to improved plaque control. Single-blind design may introduce detection bias. Small sample (n=76) limits power. Prediction: LDG likely shows modest incremental benefits on all endpoints vs fluoride control, with higher confidence for plaque/gingivitis indices than pocket depth.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT05384132 is a randomized single-blind parallel study evaluating Livfresh Dental Gel (LDG) containing EDTA as adjunct to SRP vs standard fluoride dentifrice in Stage II-III periodontitis patients. Primary endpoint: incremental PD reduction at Day 180 for sites with PD>4mm. Secondary endpoints: GI, PI, BOP reductions. No direct results available (expected 2027). Evidence from similar EDTA dentifrice study (J Periodontol 2021, PMID 33331040) showed significant PD reduction in Stage I-II maintenance patients, supporting LDG mechanism. EDTA prevents bacterial adhesion, potentially enhancing SRP outcomes. Population differences (maintenance vs active treatment) and lack of direct Phase data limit precision. SRP alone achieves 1-2mm PD reduction; adjunctive therapies typically add 0.3-0.5mm incremental benefit. GI/PI/BOP endpoints are responsive to improved plaque control. Single-blind design may introduce detection bias. Small sample (n=76) limits power. Prediction: LDG likely shows modest incremental benefits on all endpoints vs fluoride control, with higher confidence for plaque/gingivitis indices than pocket depth.

PMC Copyright notice PMCID: PMC8033283 PMID: 33837328 Scientists at the University of California Irvine's Beckman Laser Institute & Medical Clinic have conducted the first study to show that brushing with a novel toothpaste improves symptoms in patients with periodontitis. While several recent studies show that individuals with chronic gum disease are more likely to experience potentially life-threatening complications if they contract COVID-19, a new study shows promise in addressing the main issue. Researchers at the UCI Beckman Laser Institute & Medical Clinic recently reported results of a six-month long study, showing for the first time that a novel toothpaste demonstrated medically significant improvements in the health of the gums of patients with periodontitis, the most severe form of gum disease. 1 As a part of her focus on translational research, Dr Petra Wilder Smith initiated a double-blinded study testing a novel dental gel, LivFresh Dental Gel, against an FDA-approved anti-gingivitis toothpaste, to investigate their effects on gum health in patients with early to moderate periodontitis. The six-month long study compared how the two toothpastes affected periodontal pocket depths, gingival inflammation, and gum bleeding in patients with periodontitis who were in maintenance care. The findings revealed that subjects who brushed with LivFresh Dental Gel experienced clinically and statistically significant improvements in their symptoms versus the control group that brushed with an over-the-counter, FDA-approved anti-plaque, anti-gingivitis toothpaste. Several previous laboratory and clinical studies by Wilder-Smith's group have demonstrated that the novel formulation retards on a molecular level dental plaque formation, attachment and re-accumulation at the tooth surface by increasing its negative charge. The charged surface prevents early individual plaque islands from coalescing into larger deposits, discourages plaque from attaching to the tooth surface and supports the breakup of existing plaque deposits. Thus, by inhibiting dental plaque, the novel formulation reduces the presence of the harmful plaque bacteria and bacterial products that are implicated in chronic gum disease. In individuals who brushed with the test gel, pocket depths in the gums improved in more than 80% of diseased sites. Additionally, subjects who brushed with the new formulation had 2.5 times less gum inflammation and 1.9 times less gum bleeding, when compared to the group using the conventional toothpaste. Dr Wilder-Smith said: 'We anticipate that this novel formulation, when used in combination with professional periodontal care, may revolutionise healing in the gums and maintenance of periodontal health'. analysis_trace: Trial NCT05384132 evaluates LivFresh Dental Gel (2.6% EDTA) as adjunct to SRP vs SRP+standard fluoride dentifrice in Stage II-III periodontitis. Primary endpoint: incremental PD reduction at Day 180 for sites with PD>4mm. Secondary: GI, PI, BOP reductions.

Evidence from prior studies (Kaur et al. 2020, J Periodontol; Wilder-Smith group UC Irvine) shows LivFresh reduced PD by ~1.18mm vs ~0.93mm control (difference ~0.25mm) over 6 months in Stage I-II maintenance patients without SRP. Another study in Stage II-III showed significant PD, GI, PI, BOP improvements vs control.

Evidence-role assessment: Kaur 2020 (europepmc MED/33331040) = indirect_direction for primary-0; same drug, similar but milder population (Stage I-II maintenance without SRP), no SRP baseline. UC Irvine Stage II-III study (europepmc MED/31893264) = indirect_direction for all endpoints; same drug, same population severity, 6-month timeframe, but no SRP baseline.

Key mismatch: Current trial includes baseline SRP for both arms, which enhances PD reduction in both groups, potentially narrowing between-group differences. Expected result: LDG+SRP shows incremental benefit over SRP+standard paste, but effect size may be smaller than SRP-free studies.
Primary-0 prediction: LDG+SRP will show incremental PD reduction vs control at 6 months. Estimated effect: 0.3-0.5mm additional reduction at PD>4mm sites. Confidence moderate due to SRP confounding.
Secondary-0 (GI): Prior studies showed 2.5x reduction in inflammation. With SRP baseline, expect incremental GI reduction favoring LDG. Confidence moderate-high.
Secondary-1 (PI): EDTA mechanism reduces plaque adhesion. Prior studies showed significant PI reduction. Expect incremental benefit for LDG+SRP. Confidence moderate-high.
Secondary-2 (BOP): Prior studies showed 1.9x bleeding reduction. Expect incremental BOP site reduction for LDG+SRP. Confidence moderate-high.
Safety: EDTA dentifrice generally well-tolerated; no serious safety signals expected.
Overall trial prediction: Likely success on primary and secondary endpoints based on consistent prior positive results, though effect sizes may be attenuated by SRP baseline.
